messages.content: Now compare the Mission Bay resort with the downtown hotel using the Saturday arrival and Friday return. Confirm that the room works for all three of us, give me the full six-night totals, and include parking or the transportation we would actually need.

I found refundable two-queen rooms for June 14-20 at both. Mission Bay has a 410-square-foot room for three with direct beach access; the quoted bay-view category has a balcony. Its six-night lodging total is $2,202.75: $1,674 room charge, $224.32 lodging tax, $270 mandatory resort charge, and $34.43 tax on that charge. Self-parking adds $288, bringing the stay to $2,490.75. The downtown room is smaller at 335 square feet but also allows three guests in two queens. Breakfast for three is included. Its total is $1,714.61: $1,512 room charge and $202.61 tax, with no required destination charge.
Does the downtown total include parking? We are not renting a car, so price rideshares instead.

No parking is included in either comparison now. For Mission Bay, airport rideshares plus one downtown round trip for the harbor reservation should be about $80 total. For downtown, airport rideshares plus four beach round trips are about $238. That makes the practical hotel-and-local-transport totals $2,282.75 for Mission Bay and $1,952.61 downtown. Downtown remains $330.14 less.
Why only four beach round trips downtown?

I counted Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday as beach days. Saturday is the harbor reservation after arrival, Tuesday is the zoo day, and Friday morning is left for breakfast and a short downtown activity before heading to the airport. Adding another beach day would raise the downtown transportation estimate by about $42.
That itinerary is right. What are the deposit and cancellation terms for each rate? I do not want a headline saying refundable if the useful deadlines are very different.

Mission Bay takes a $356.46 deposit on May 15, equal to the first night with its allocated taxes and resort charge. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. Pacific on June 7; after that, the deposit is forfeited. Downtown takes a $285.77 first-night deposit on June 7. It can be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. Pacific on June 11, after which one night is charged. Both balances are due at checkout.
Check the room details more closely. Is the Mission Bay balcony guaranteed in the category you priced, and is breakfast included there?

The bay-view two-queen category explicitly lists a furnished balcony, so it is guaranteed by room type rather than treated as a request. It accommodates up to four. Breakfast is not included; the resort credit included in the mandatory charge is limited to $15 per room per day and cannot cover breakfast for three.
And downtown? Any balcony or view, and what exactly does breakfast for three mean?

The downtown two-queen room has a city view, but no balcony is promised. The breakfast package provides three daily buffet vouchers, including on Friday morning. Taxes and gratuities for the buffet are included. The room record allows three occupants, so there is no extra-person fee for your daughter.

For scenic family stays, keep looking for a balcony when it is available because we spend real downtime at the hotel. A first-floor room is different, though: I am fine without a balcony if it has convenient outdoor access. Do not eliminate an otherwise good coastal hotel just because no balcony is available.

Understood. For this comparison, the Mission Bay room has the stronger setting for hotel downtime and a guaranteed balcony. The downtown room still qualifies on occupancy, breakfast, flexibility, and price despite having no balcony.

The resort cost still looks high. Add meals so we are not pretending the $15 credit solves breakfast. Use the same $720 meal estimate from the downtown plan, then adjust only what the included breakfasts or resort credit genuinely replace.

Using $720 as the baseline, downtown breakfast replaces an estimated $120, leaving $600 for meals. At Mission Bay, six $15 credits replace $90, leaving $630. With activities at $249 and the selected flights at $1,011, the working trip totals become $4,494.75 for Mission Bay and $3,812.61 downtown. The resort version is $682.14 more overall.
That is a real difference, but downtown creates eight beach rides. Are those rideshare estimates conservative enough for three people and beach gear?

They assume a standard rideshare at roughly $21 each way, including a modest surge allowance. Three people and ordinary beach bags should fit, but not bulky equipment. Raising each beach round trip to $50 would add $32 across four days, making downtown $3,844.61 and narrowing the gap to $650.14. Mission Bay still needs only airport rides and the harbor round trip.
Compare the non-price tradeoff plainly. We are there for a coastal vacation, not a downtown weekend with occasional beach visits.

Mission Bay fits the trip better: the beach is available without coordinating a car, Friday morning can be spent on the water, and the larger room and balcony make downtime easier. Downtown gives you the later cancellation deadline, included full breakfasts, and simpler access to the harbor and zoo, but four beach days require eight rides and carrying everything back and forth. The question is whether that convenience and setting justify roughly $650-$682 more.
They do. Reserve Mission Bay in the refundable bay-view two-queen room for three. No rental car and no parking. Make sure the 14-year-old is listed, and do not touch the flights yet.

Before I finalize: the reservation will be June 14-20 for two adults and one 14-year-old in the refundable bay-view room with two queen beds and a furnished balcony. The lodging total is $2,202.75, with a $356.46 deposit scheduled for May 15 and the balance due at checkout. Free cancellation ends June 7 at 6:00 p.m. Pacific. Shall I place it on those terms?
Yes, book that exact room and rate.

Mission Bay is reserved for June 14-20 for two adults and one 14-year-old in a bay-view room with two queen beds and a furnished balcony. Confirmation MB-61483 shows $2,202.75 total: $1,674 room, $224.32 lodging tax, $270 resort charge, and $34.43 charge tax. A $356.46 deposit is due May 15; the remainder is due at checkout. Cancellation is free through June 7 at 6:00 p.m. Pacific. No car or parking was added. The working trip estimate is $4,494.75: $1,011 flights, $2,202.75 hotel, $80 rideshares, $249 activities, and $630 meals. Only the hotel is booked. Flights, airport and harbor rides, activities, and meals remain unbooked or estimated.
